output.title: Rounding claims in a one-person business
output.body:
If you run a one-person business, the real question is not whether AI can “handle claims.” It is whether the rounding work is repetitive enough to become a bounded workflow instead of a fresh judgment call every time.

Use a simple rule. Keep it manual if each case needs new context, exceptions, or owner judgement. Consider AI only for a narrow support step if the same checks keep repeating, such as sorting items, comparing fields, or flagging mismatches before you review them. Final approval stays with you. That is the control boundary. No robot gets to sign off on your money or liability, and frankly that is a reasonable design choice.

One practical next step is to map one week of the current process by hand. Write down the trigger, the inputs, the rule you apply, where rounding happens, and where you stop to check manually. Then mark which part is truly repeatable. If the rule can be written clearly, it may be a candidate for support. If it depends on judgement every time, manual review remains the right default.

The useful filter is not “Can AI do it?” but “Which part is stable enough to standardise without giving up owner control?”
